findings.observation: The added review-status card and three-step rail displace the exact quote and vermilion causal seam from the initial fact-decision viewport. In the candidate fact capture, the user sees generic progress chrome and the fact tray, while the selected Direction 2 target showed source, seam, and proposed change as one continuous composition.
findings.evidence: post/fact.png (sha256 d9d4e6fa7606a69d31657448b48318baa25221e1c2d06adc5e1ea3a83d1fe86e) compared with prototype/source-visual.png (sha256 98f9704aa341ee3f8535161149670487a9702b67ffda3a29c64ff5f85b4bb53d); current Prototype.tsx:382-417 inserts ReviewStagePanel before ReviewSession; prototype.css:136-149 gives it full card materiality, while prototype.css:183 fixes a 370px decision tray over the lower viewport.
findings.user_impact: At the consequential fact decision, visual attention shifts from why the change is supported to process narration. The recruiter must scroll or rely on memory to reconnect evidence with the decision, weakening the product's most ownable evidence-to-change visual grammar.
findings.recommendation: Collapse progress into a compact inline state marker or the tray header, and restore a 393x852 composition in which the exact quote, causal seam, state diff, and primary fact decision are simultaneously legible.
findings.verification: Render the fact state at 393x852 with the long name; without scrolling, the exact source quote, vermilion seam, Unknown-to-date diff, and Confirm/Edit/Not supported decision group must all remain visibly connected.

findings.observation: Decision-relevant provenance and guardrail copy is repeatedly set as 10-11px uppercase text with wide tracking. The Today proof line and approval guardrail pills read more like fine-print disclaimers than inspectable evidence and effect boundaries.
findings.evidence: tightened/today-fixed.png and post/approval.png; prototype.css:86-87, 94, 101, 105, 170, 195, and 210 define multiple 10-11px tracked labels across proof, context, source, edit, and effect metadata.
findings.user_impact: The primary headlines remain clear, but the exact source/effect qualifiers that establish trust lose hierarchy and are difficult to scan on the 393px mobile target.
findings.recommendation: Raise consequential metadata to a durable mobile reading size, reduce all-caps tracking, and consolidate repeated boundary language so provenance and exact effect read as part of the decision rather than footnotes.
findings.verification: Re-render Today, fact, and approval at 393x852; source, date, scope, and exact-effect qualifiers should remain comfortably readable at native scale and preserve measured contrast in light and dark themes.

findings.observation: The tightened Today capture restores the primary decision CTA, but the fixed global composer visually collides with the next-section boundary: the 'Next' label and count are clipped into the bottom/home-indicator region instead of forming an intentional continuation cue.
findings.evidence: tightened/today-fixed.png (sha256 f4db212f8acc17460fd11d66b6e55b10be1ce1108a4e43dd4efb3c1a48eae308); prototype.css:125-129 fixes the composer above the safe area while the lead card, secondary action, and continuation section remain in the same scroll composition.
findings.user_impact: The lead item is understandable, but the first viewport ends with a visibly broken crop that makes the interface feel less resolved and obscures the transition from one lead dependency to the remaining work.
findings.recommendation: End the initial viewport cleanly above the fixed composer or expose a deliberate, unobstructed continuation affordance; do not leave section text partially covered by the composer or home-indicator zone.
findings.verification: At 393x852 from scroll position zero, no heading, count, action, or row text intersects the composer or safe-area region; after one scroll gesture, the Next heading and first continuation row appear intact.

strengths: The warm neutral palette, restrained vermilion, serif/sans pairing, and low-shadow materiality are recognizably Talent Signal rather than generic AI decoration.
The exact-effect approval tray is unusually clear and calm: one strong action, explicit target/when/effect structure, and no competing outreach control.
Ambiguous, unknown, verified, and AX5 dark states preserve human dignity and avoid candidate scoring; state changes use text and iconography rather than color alone.
missing_evidence: No freeze-candidate.json is present to bind one exact screenshot set and current code hash; post/today.png and tightened/today-fixed.png are materially different Today states.
The current Prototype.tsx and prototype.css modification times postdate the supplied post and tightened screenshots, so the latest code state is not represented by a matching frozen render.
open_questions: Which Today capture and source hashes define the candidate under review: post/today.png or tightened/today-fixed.png plus the later current prototype code?
